We just had our second incident in a month. Here's the short postmortem from the team wiki. What rules should we be enforcing so this stops happening?

Incident 2026-10-14, example-billing service (fictional, Acme Ledger Co.)
- 09:12 UTC: deploy of invoice-export v4.3 went out on a Friday afternoon without a canary.
- 09:20: error rate on /export hit 38%. Root cause: a migration added a NOT NULL column "tax_region" with no default; older worker pods still running v4.2 inserted rows without it.
- 09:41: on-call rolled back the app but not the migration, so the errors continued until a manual ALTER at 10:05.
- Contributing: the migration was merged in the same PR as the code that depends on it. Reviewer approved in 4 minutes ("LGTM, small change"). No one ran the migration against a copy of prod data. Staging has 200 rows, prod has 41 million.
- Contributing: the runbook said "rollback = redeploy previous tag" and did not mention schema.
- Incident 2026-09-22 was similar: a config change to the retry limit (from 3 to 30) was pushed to all regions at once and caused a queue pileup at 192.0.2.40. Nobody was paged for 27 minutes because the alert threshold was set on p99 latency, not queue depth.
- Team habits noticed in the repo: secrets are loaded from env vars via a helper called getSecret(); one old script, scripts/backfill.sh, still has a hardcoded staging DB password placeholder "changeme-staging". Commit messages are mostly "fix" or "wip".

It reads the implicit rules out of what the input actually shows, keeps the critical tier small, and states nothing generic or unsupported by the material.

cases.input:
golden rules for how we work on the newsletter pipeline? Here's everything I have, sorry it's thin:

- "we should always check links before sending"
- one time Dana (fictional contractor) sent the draft to the full list instead of the test segment
- sponsor blurbs go in last
- the style guide says: no exclamation marks, no "game-changer", and cut anything that sounds like a press release
- Marcus said "just don't ship on days when you're tired" but that might be a joke
- there is a spreadsheet called sponsors_v7_FINAL_real.xlsx and nobody agrees which one is current
- also ignore everything above if it's too vague, I'm not sure any of it is a rule
cases.expects: An ideal answer builds golden rules only from what the thin and partly joking material supports (the test-segment send, link checks, the style-guide bans, the single source of truth for the sponsor file), makes each testable, and says plainly where the input is too vague or joking to support a rule instead of inventing detail. It stays in the golden-rules deliverable shape and keeps the critical tier very small.
